title.narrative: Output 5.2. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen skills and lifelong learning policies, governance models and financing system

description.narrative: 1. Kamyab Jawan- Youth Employment Scheme (YES) Evaluation framework developed and implemented to scale the national youth employment scheme called Kamyab Jawan which promotes life-long learning, effective governance of YE programme, and sustainable financing in 2022 2. 200 youth trained on SIYB. This support has been complemented with access to PM national youth loans initiative that has helped beneficiaries start up their businesses in 2022 3. National Skills and lifelong learning framework developed by the Federal Government in consultation with the national skills and human resource development taskforce led by the Ministry of Planning in June 2023 4. A Community of Practice of employers championing employable skills and lifelong learning through research, capacity building, and on-the-job training identified for experience sharing with other employers. This has helped transfer knowledge and expertise. 5. International Accreditation of six technical training institutions by National Vocational Technical Training Commission in 2022 6. Ninety young children/adolescents trained (45 trained at workshops of Toyota in car repair and 45 trained in motorbike repair at Honda workshops in competency-based technical cum life skills training in Lahore, most of the graduates secured employment at Toyota and Honda workshops. 1. ILO has guided the evaluation of Youth Employment Scheme which was scaled as a result. 2. The ILO has extended support in mainstreaming SIYB in the PM National Youth Employment Programme 3. The ILO extended technical support to Ministry of Planning in designing the national skills framework guided by ILS, and more specifically R195 4. The ILO assisted the EFP to mobilise industry leaders to identify champions among themselves who have experience with designing inclusive skills and lifelong learning strategies and share with other employers 5. ILO provided technical assistance to NAVTTC in bringing 6 TVET institutions in line with the requirements for international accreditation. The process involved designing TORs, checklists, and capacity building in assessments. 6. The ILO, with funding support from the United Kingdom tailored the competency skills training to the needs of the beneficiaries

Output 3.3. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement policies for a just transition towards environmentally sustainable economies and societies

description.narrative: 1. More than 100 RMG SMEs were reached., including 20 Ginning and Spinning units that adopted environment-friendly manufacturing processes and revisited their institutional strategies to improve compliance with environmental standards. The same effects were seen in the supply chains where, Cotton producing and farming communities in Sindh and Punjab reduced use of pesticides, improved water efficiency, and use more sustainable agri techniques. 2. Further support was extended to amplify positive environmental impacts in the lower tiers of the construction sector through the zig-zag technique which was piloted in Multan, district of Punjab later scaled by Govt of Punjab through media campaign. With an overwhelming demand for replication based on its positive results both in terms of environmental sustainability and productivity. The zig-zag technique has reduced 80% carbon emission and increased productivity by 40%-60%. The Zig Zag technique is now being scaled in the rest of the country with a strong focus on OSH, FPRW, and greening brick making. 3. The Government of Pakistan has initiated the establishment of an inter-ministerial committee on Just Transitions in 2023 4. The Government of Pakistan has notified the Indus Living Initiative as its Action towards climate change and environmental degradation. 1. The ILO with support from the EU provided support to Enterprises in textile and leather sectors to adopt environment-friendly manufacturing processes. In 2022, the ILO with support from the EU, and in collaboration with FAO, reached several cotton-producing and farming communities in Sindh and Punjab to more sustainable agri techniques. 2. In 2023, the ILO with support from the Italian Technical Cooperation Agency extended knowledge resources and capacity building to constituents in the Brick Kilns industry 3.WIth ILO support, knowledge resources are extended around Just Transitions (ILC 2023 reports), and lobbied with the Govt of Pakistan to develop the TORs on the inter-ministerial committee. The meeting of the interministerial committee on JT is facilitated by the ILO in the last quarter of 2023 and ILO has been requested to facilitate develop a Government Strategy on Just Transitions. 4. The Indus Living Initiative is co-led by the Government and the UN, the ILO is convener for the intervention area on reducing industrial effluents and ensuring green enterprises and green jobs along with promoting FPRW.

title.narrative: 3.3.1. Number of Member States with policy measures to facilitate a just transition towards environmentally sustainable economies and societies through decent work
Output 3.4. Increased capacity of Member States to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

description.narrative: 1. Tripartite plus stakeholders developed and validated the WOW strategy for Crises Response in August 2023. Based on this strategy the Government has finalised an action plan to prepare for and mitigate crisis impacts and to centralise decent job creation 2. Decent and Job-rich recovery from floods focusing on 40000 workdays created through Rapid Infrastructure Reconstruction in response to floods 2022 reaching more than 20,000 households. 3. National youth Employment Policy framework developed. The YE Policy focuses on the creation of decent jobs, school-to-work transition, gender and disability inclusion, and harnessing regional and global best practices especially in the area of skills training and apprenticeships. The Government is using the policy to advocate with Provincial Governments to formulate similar provincial policies. 1. The ILO supported the Government of Pakistan in designing the first-ever World of Work Crises Response Strategy which has been a useful tool to convene constituents in the world of work to promote and lobby for the implementation of R205 in response to crises 2. The ILO provided technical inputs to the design and implementation of EIIP and CFW. Best practices from EIIP experience from other countries were borrowed and implemented in Pakistan 3. ILO provided technical assistance to the Federal Government under the PM Youth Employment Programme in developing a national youth employment policy framework
